correctness.rationale: The exact FEx-G CDF algebraically reduces to survival (exp(s^(1-s))-1)/(e-1). Expanding s^(1-s) at s=0 gives the stated constant tail equivalence and second-order term. Differentiating the exact survival map yields an explicit hazard-ratio factor whose two factors both tend to one. Positive-moment equivalence follows from two-sided eventual comparison of the survival functions and the tail-integral moment identity. The packaged checker independently verifies the limits and the Pareto quantile constant.

value.rationale: Tail behavior is explicitly presented as part of the new family's flexibility. The theorem identifies a sharp structural limit on that flexibility: extreme upper-tail order, hazard scale, and positive-moment thresholds are inherited from the baseline. This matters for reliability and heavy-tail use because choosing the transform cannot repair a baseline with the wrong moment boundary or extreme-tail index, even though it may improve central fit and hazard shape.
